title: Tips and the extra half of overtime pay get a tax break through 2028
reason: Fails the net-impact test: a sweetener in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was paid for largely by cutting Medicaid and SNAP (CBO: ~10M more uninsured by 2034). Belongs with harms, sweeteners noted.

title: Babies born 2025 through 2028 get $1,000 invested in their name
reason: Fails the net-impact test: carried in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which was paid for largely by cutting Medicaid and SNAP. Belongs with harms, sweeteners noted.

title: Virginia Beach lowered its property tax rate to 97 cents
reason: Fails the net-impact test: a 2-cent rate cut for owners paired with a $36.60/yr flat trash-fee increase that renters' households also pay; the median owner's bill still rose.

title: Norfolk's Tidewater Gardens is being rebuilt as new mixed-income homes
reason: Owner's call: public housing redevelopment with displacement (618 units demolished; 330 physical replacements plus 288 vouchers; 44 of 334 families returned). Out of scope for a wins site until harms are covered.

title: Newport News is replacing Ridley Place with hundreds of new homes
reason: Owner's call: public housing redevelopment with displacement risk and low return rates. Out of scope for a wins site until harms are covered.

title: Settle old city violation fines with no interest through Jan. 10
reason: Owner's call: fine amnesty with no size limit; relief mostly to property and business owners, including large landlords.

title: A regional tax is paying to double the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel
reason: Owner's call: funded by regressive regional sales and fuel taxes; buys highway lanes (some tolled) and no transit; benefit still under construction.

title: Fort Monroe's historic grounds in Hampton are a national monument
reason: Owner's call: low direct impact on working people.

title: Smartphones stay put away from first bell to last in New York schools
reason: Owner's call: no money, service, or right for working people; low impact.

title: Virginia's state grocery tax is gone; only a 1% local tax remains
reason: Fails the net-impact test (owner's call after GPT verification): the state never replaced the transportation revenue it cut, a recurring loss (about $741M over six years), and groceries bought with SNAP or WIC were already exempt, so the lowest-income shoppers got nothing.
